title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 48
paragraphs: The Ister, the greatest of all the rivers we know, flows always with equal volume in summer and in winter alike. It is the first of the Scythian rivers towards the west, and it has become the greatest of all rivers because other rivers flow into it. These are the ones that make it great. Five in number are those which flow through the Scythian land: the one the Scythians call Porata and the Hellenes Pyretos, and besides this, Tiarantos, Araros, Naparis, and Ordessos. The first-mentioned is a great river lying to the east, and there it joins its waters with the Ister. The second, Tiarantos, is more to the west and smaller. The Araros, Naparis, and Ordessos flow into the Ister running between these two.
